title: Niemann-Pick disease (sphingomyelinase deficiency): cherry-red macula + splenomegaly
vignette: A couple comes to the clinic for preconception counseling. They are offered genetic screening because they are of Ashkenazi Jewish descent. Test results show that both are carriers for a lysosomal enzyme deficiency disorder that results in decreased metabolic degradation of a phospholipid substrate to ceramide, which leads to a buildup of the phospholipid. They are counseled about the chance that their offspring will be affected by this disorder. The couple wants to know the clinical features of an affected child. Which of the following findings would be most consistent with this condition?

clues.note: Several lysosomal storage diseases (Niemann-Pick, Tay-Sachs, Gaucher) are more common in the Ashkenazi Jewish population (founder effect).

clues.text: decreased metabolic degradation of a phospholipid substrate to ceramide
clues.note: An enzyme that degrades a PHOSPHOLIPID (sphingomyelin) to ceramide is SPHINGOMYELINASE; its deficiency = Niemann-Pick disease.
Accumulation of sphingomyelin (a phospholipid) in cells - forming foamy, lipid-laden macrophages - characterizes Niemann-Pick disease.

whatMatters: Deficient degradation of a PHOSPHOLIPID (sphingomyelin) to ceramide = SPHINGOMYELINASE deficiency = NIEMANN-PICK disease. It causes accumulation of sphingomyelin with hepatosplenomegaly, progressive neurodegeneration, and a cherry-red macula (RETINAL OPACIFICATION). The consistent findings are RETINAL OPACIFICATION and SPLENOMEGALY. Answer D.
strategy: Use the substrate: sphingomyelin (a phospholipid) -> ceramide is done by sphingomyelinase (Niemann-Pick). Recall its features: hepatosplenomegaly, neurodegeneration/hypotonia, foamy macrophages, and a cherry-red macula (retinal opacification). Pick 'retinal opacification and splenomegaly.' Reject dysostosis multiplex/coarse features + corneal clouding (Hurler - a mucopolysaccharidosis), coarse features + cardiac dysfunction (Hunter/MPS), neuropathic pain + angiokeratomas (Fabry), and small stature/infertility (Bloom syndrome).

options.text: Abnormally shaped bones and corneal clouding
Coarse facial features and cardiac dysfunction

eliminations.label: Bone deformities + corneal clouding - Hurler (mucopolysaccharidosis)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: dysostosis multiplex (abnormal bones) with CORNEAL CLOUDING = Hurler syndrome (alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency; accumulates glycosaminoglycans - a polysaccharide, not phospholipid). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the substrate here is a phospholipid (sphingomyelin), pointing to Niemann-Pick, not a mucopolysaccharidosis. ✅ Correct if: MPS with corneal clouding (Hurler).

eliminations.label: Coarse features + cardiac dysfunction - Hunter/MPS
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: coarse facies and multiorgan involvement of the mucopolysaccharidoses (e.g., Hunter). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: MPS accumulate glycosaminoglycans (polysaccharide), not sphingomyelin. ✅ Correct if: a mucopolysaccharidosis (heparan/dermatan sulfate).

eliminations.label: Neuropathic pain + angiokeratomas - Fabry disease
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: Fabry disease (alpha-galactosidase A deficiency; accumulates globotriaosylceramide) with neuropathic pain, angiokeratomas, and renal/cardiac disease. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: Fabry's substrate is not sphingomyelin, and it is X-linked; the phospholipid-to-ceramide clue is Niemann-Pick. ✅ Correct if: X-linked Fabry with angiokeratomas.

eliminations.label: Small stature + infertility - Bloom syndrome
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: Bloom syndrome (chromosomal instability) with growth failure, sun-sensitive rash, and cancer predisposition. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it involves DNA repair/instability, not phospholipid accumulation. ✅ Correct if: chromosomal-instability syndrome.

reasoning: Deficient degradation of a phospholipid (sphingomyelin) to ceramide = sphingomyelinase deficiency
Features include hepatosplenomegaly, neurodegeneration, foamy macrophages, and a cherry-red macula (retinal opacification)
-> retinal opacification and splenomegaly; answer D
mechanism: Niemann-Pick disease is an autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficiency of SPHINGOMYELINASE, the enzyme that degrades the PHOSPHOLIPID sphingomyelin to ceramide. Without it, sphingomyelin accumulates within lysosomes, producing enlarged, foamy, lipid-laden macrophages ('foam cells') that infiltrate the liver (HEPATOMEGALY), spleen (SPLENOMEGALY), and CNS. Affected infants develop after a period of normal early development and then regress, with progressive NEURODEGENERATION and hypotonia; accumulation in the retinal ganglion cells produces a CHERRY-RED MACULA (retinal opacification). The classic (type A) form is usually fatal by ~age 3. Like Tay-Sachs and Gaucher, it has increased incidence in the Ashkenazi Jewish population (founder effect), so carrier screening is offered preconceptionally. Thus the consistent findings are retinal opacification (cherry-red macula) and splenomegaly. The distractors describe other inborn errors: mucopolysaccharidoses (Hurler - corneal clouding; Hunter - coarse features), Fabry (angiokeratomas/neuropathic pain), and Bloom (small stature/instability).

difficulty.text: First Aid Biochem > Niemann-Pick: sphingomyelinase deficiency; sphingomyelin accumulation; hepatosplenomegaly, neurodegeneration, foam cells, cherry-red macula; Ashkenazi Jewish; contrast Tay-Sachs (no hepatosplenomegaly), Gaucher, Fabry, MPS.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Phospholipid (sphingomyelin) -> ceramide block = Niemann-Pick -> cherry-red macula + hepatosplenomegaly.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on sphingomyelinase, sphingomyelin, cherry-red macula, foam cells, or mucopolysaccharidosis? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Corneal clouding/coarse features = mucopolysaccharidoses (Hurler/Hunter); angiokeratomas = Fabry; small stature/instability = Bloom.
